fixtures.rationale: applyDiscount assigns to a property of the order parameter directly, so the caller's order object is changed by the call.
addLineItem pushes into the items array it received instead of returning a new array, so the caller's array grows in place.
markShipped assigns through a nested property path rooted at the order parameter, mutating a value the caller still holds.
recordVisit calls set on the counts Map it received as a parameter, changing what every other holder of that Map sees.
stripSecrets deletes a property directly on the user parameter instead of returning a copy without that property.
sortByDate calls the in-place sort method on the events array it received, reordering the caller's own array.
applyDiscount spreads order into a new object and returns that copy; no property of the order parameter is ever assigned.
sortByDate slices events into a local copy first and sorts that copy, leaving the events parameter itself untouched.

groupBy builds its own local Map and never assigns through or calls a mutating method on the items or keyOf parameters themselves; two known false negatives are out of scope for this collector: a reduce callback's accumulator is not a top-level function parameter, and an alias such as `const r = record; r.x = 1` hides the mutation behind a local binding.
response is a builder object the caller passed in specifically to be filled by setting headers on it, which is writeHeaders's documented job rather than an unexpected side effect.
The parameter is destructured and renamed to current; assigning current.status changes the caller's order object, so the rename does not hide the mutation.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
